entries.title: Judges 4:1
segments: When restraint is removed, notwithstanding all divine favors men will continue in sin, and often be guilty of the grossest transgressions.

entries.title: Judges 4:2
segments: Hazor--Harosheth; cities in the north part of Canaan in and around which many of the remaining Canaanites lived.

entries.title: Judges 4:3
segments: Oft-repeated iniquities bring upon their perpetrators greatly increased calamities.

entries.title: Judges 4:5
segments: Mount Ephraim; the hill country of Ephraim.

entries.title: Judges 4:6
segments:
Kedesh-naphtali; so called to distingush it from two other cities called Kedesh, one in Issachar and one in Judah. 
 
  Mount Tabor; on the north-east border of the plain of Jezreel.

entries.title: Judges 4:7
segments:
The river Kishon; which rises at the base of mount Tabor, runs through the plain of Jezreel, and empties into the Mediterranean at the bay of Acre. 
 
When men cry unto the Lord in their trouble, he can, and often does grant them relief; and in receiving it they should hear his voice saying, Sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.

entries.title: Judges 4:9
segments: Want of confidence in God, and of readiness to undertake that to which he calls, brings dishonor, and deprives men of many blessings which they might otherwise enjoy.

entries.title: Judges 4:10
segments:
Called Zebulun and Naphtali; the men of war from those tribes. 
 
  Went up; to mount Tabor.

entries.title: Judges 4:11
segments: Had several himself; the Kenites lived in the south part of the country, but Heber had left them and removed to the north.

entries.title: Judges 4:13
segments: Men, from pride and the indulgence of wicked passions, often engage in projects which God designs shall be for their ruin.

entries.title: Judges 4:15
segments: Though men are the means, God is the author of success, and to him belongs the glory.

entries.title: Judges 4:21
segments:
Nail of the tent; a large spike or pin, which was driven into the ground to fasten the cords of a tent. 
 
When the enemies of God and the oppressors of his people say, Peace and safety, sudden destruction may come upon them from which there can beno escape.

entries.title: Judges 4:23
segments: Things which God in his providence accomplishes through the instrumentality of men, are in the Bible ascribed to him as really as if no agency but his had been employed; and they are also inscribed to men as really as if men alone had performed them; thus showing that divine and human agency harmoniously cooperate, and that men are workers together with God when they obey him and thus work out their salvation, he working in them to will and to do of his own good pleasure.
